problem: Existing RL human-following methods fold proximity, human safety and obstacle safety into one dense weighted reward, so the proximity-safety trade-off is implicit, hard to tune, and may not generalize to unfamiliar pedestrian behaviors in dense crowds.
motivation: Following a moving target means any detour for safety risks losing the target, so the robot must balance proximity against safety in dense crowds. Reward weights do not map predictably to behavior, and a fixed trade-off learned in training may fail under OOD pedestrian motion.
key_idea: Decompose human following into a sparse task reward plus three independent cost constraints (following, human safety, obstacle safety) optimized with PPO-Lagrangian, with ACI-based human-motion prediction uncertainty fed into both the observations and the human safety cost.
insight: Cost thresholds map predictably onto behavior: moving from safety-conservative to aggressive-following profiles lowers AFD from 2.54 to 2.23 and TLR from 10.08% to 3.20% while human CR rises from 8.80% to 14.24%. Reward-weight tuning in RL+ACI is erratic: doubling w_F leaves AFD at 2.26 and worsens both TLR and human CR. Ablations show ACI observations help (RL to RL+ACI) and the decomposition adds further gains (RL+ACI to Ours).
method: Constraint decomposition (CMDP): sparse reward for success/collision/target-lost; separate costs for following (equality constraint, target level δF), human safety (≤δH) and obstacle safety (≤δO), each with its own critic

Cost functions: following cost is linear in distance beyond d_personal=1.0 m; human cost is the max intrusion depth into safety regions around current and K' predicted positions; obstacle cost is linear below d_safe_o=0.5 m
ACI uncertainty: M parallel adaptive conformal estimators give online per-human, per-horizon error bounds, which enter the human tokens and set the radii of the predicted-position safety regions

Policy network: 3D CNN over 5 steps of local occupancy grids, with robot, target, obstacle and human tokens early-fused in a 4-layer, 8-head Transformer; the robot token output drives the actor, and humans are ordered by distance with masking for undetected ones

PPO-Lagrangian: four critics with GAE; advantages combined with Lagrange multipliers and normalized by (1+Σλ); multipliers updated by dual gradient descent (the following multiplier is not clipped at 0 because of the equality constraint)
Sim and deployment: CrowdNav extended with static obstacles (40 humans, ORCA); real robot ROSMASTER X3 with 2D LiDAR, DR-SPAAM detection, SORT tracking, CV prediction and ACI

setting.backbone: Custom 3D-CNN + Transformer encoder actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO-Lagrangian)
setting.training_data: Self-generated simulated CrowdNav episodes with random static obstacles and 40 ORCA humans (RL from scratch); no external data
setting.observation: Robot state, target and human positions with CV-predicted trajectories and ACI uncertainties, local occupancy grid maps (last 5 steps); LiDAR-derived in the real world
setting.privileged: none (simulation uses ground-truth human states as input to the predictor; the real robot uses LiDAR detection and tracking)

numbers.extra: 1250 samples across 5 seeds; best tuned configuration

numbers_note: Real-robot result (7 of 10 trajectories successful) is given in text only. The benchmark is a custom simulator, so the bench names are 'other:'.
results: In-distribution the method reaches 78.08% SR and 16.16% CR, beating OGM-HEIGHT (52.32% SR) and the ablations RL (68.00%) and RL+ACI (71.60%). It also leads in SR across all four OOD settings (e.g. corridor 89.76% vs 82.96% for RL+ACI and 56.24% for OGM-HEIGHT). On the real robot it completes 7 of 10 trials.
limitations: Real-world failures (3 of 10) stem from upstream perception errors and a target faster than the robot; the policy breaks in dense, fast crowds with sudden turns and tight groups
Thresholds must be hand-tuned per behavioral profile, and human preferences are not adapted to
Uses a simple CV predictor and a 2D LiDAR setup; evaluated only in a custom 2D simulator, not photorealistic or 3D environments
